investigator.method: Level 1 PASSIVE_STATIC only: plain curl GET (descriptive User-Agent, no authentication, no browser) of the venue's official homepage/programme page and three real, currently-listed individual event pages. Each individual event page directly embeds a single schema.org MusicEvent JSON-LD block — no per-page crawling logic beyond following the homepage's own listed event links was needed.

probe_history.reason: The venue's own homepage (which doubles as its 'Program' page per its own nav) is server-rendered and lists every upcoming event as a plain <a href="/events/{slug}"> link (no JSON-LD on the listing page itself). Following three of those real, currently-listed links to their own individual event pages showed each one embeds a single, consistently-shaped schema.org MusicEvent JSON-LD block (name, startDate, url, location) directly in the server-rendered HTML — sufficient to answer the investigation question without any structural/browser escalation.

venue_reference: Lido Berlin (concert venue and club, Cuvrystraße 7, Kreuzberg, Berlin — run by the Festsaal Kreuzberg team, alongside Bi Nuu and Astra Kulturhaus)

identity.notes: Official identity confirmed directly from the retained evidence at https://www.lido-berlin.de/ — its own footer states its own address (Cuvrystraße 7, 10997 Berlin), phone, and email (info@lido-berlin.de), and links to its own verified social accounts (facebook.com/lidoberlin, instagram.com/lidoberlin). The footer also links to binuu.de and astra-berlin.de as sibling venues under the same Festsaal Kreuzberg operator, consistent with independent third-party discovery leads.

site_classification.platform: A Ruby on Rails application (X-Powered-By: Phusion Passenger, X-Runtime header observed). No CMS/plugin fingerprint beyond this; each individual event detail page (not the listing page) embeds its own schema.org MusicEvent JSON-LD.

title.notes: Each event detail page's own JSON-LD 'name' field (e.g. 'SHAKEY GRAVES', 'JORJA SMITH', 'BUZZCOCKS'), confirmed identical across all 3 sampled events.

start_date.notes: Each event detail page's own JSON-LD 'startDate', a full ISO 8601 datetime with an explicit UTC offset (e.g. '2026-08-26T20:00:00+00:00'). IMPORTANT CAVEAT, honestly recorded rather than silently corrected: the stated '+00:00' offset does not match Berlin's actual summer offset (CEST, +02:00) for an August/September date, and the time-of-day component (e.g. 20:00) exactly matches the venue's own separately-rendered local start-time text on the same page (confirmed for event 1: JSON-LD says 20:00, the page's own visible 'Doors ... 20:00' text block also says 20:00) — this strongly suggests the site always hardcodes '+00:00' regardless of true local offset, i.e. the time-of-day digits are reliable local wall-clock time but the stated offset annotation itself should not be trusted as genuine UTC without further verification. A real collector should treat this as FLOATING_LOCAL time (Europe/Berlin) rather than a genuine UTC instant.

time.notes: Time-of-day portion of the same 'startDate' field; corroborated by the page's own separately-rendered 'Doors'/start-time text block for event 1 (both say 20:00). See start_date notes for the offset caveat.

end.notes: No 'endDate' or equivalent field is present in the JSON-LD block on any of the 3 sampled events.

venue_location.notes: Each event's own JSON-LD 'location.name'/'location.address' — the literal string 'Lido Berlin' with the address 'Cuvrystraße 7, 10997 Berlin', identical on all 3 sampled events.

source_record_id.notes: No numeric or opaque id field is exposed anywhere in the JSON-LD. Each event's own 'url' field is a permanent-looking '/events/{date-slug}' path (e.g. '/events/2026-08-26-shakey-graves') that this source itself uses as the record's own canonical address, matching the LAV/Moog precedent (ingestion/lav/discovery.mjs, moog-barcelona-01) of treating a source's own URL slug as source_record_id. Left PARTIAL rather than PROVEN here because, unlike Moog's case, this was not independently stress-tested against a genuinely re-observed/re-fetched instance of the same event within this bounded investigation (no repeated observation over time was performed) — a future offline-proof step should verify slug stability before promoting this to PROVEN.

price.notes: No price/offers field is present in the JSON-LD on any of the 3 sampled events; ticket links observed elsewhere on the page point to eventim.de (third-party ticketing), not a first-party price field.

reasons: Identity PROVEN directly from retained first-party evidence.
acquisition_class JSON_LD_EVENT, a resolved supported class, consistent across 3 independently sampled events.
A CONFIRMED public data path retained: the homepage's own event links, each leading to a JSON-LD-bearing detail page.
title, start_date, venue_location and event_url all PROVEN via basis DIRECT_SOURCE.

source_record_id left honestly PARTIAL (URL-slug strategy plausible per existing project precedent, but not independently stress-tested within this investigation) and start_date carries an explicitly documented offset caveat rather than a silently 'corrected' value — both are exactly the kind of detail an offline-proof/collector-build follow-up step should resolve before any activation decision, which this investigation deliberately does not attempt (no collector code or DETERMINISTIC_DERIVATION offline-proof evidence was produced in this task).
recommended_family JSON_LD (an existing, already-implemented, reusable module — ingestion/json-ld/).
